## Progress by stage

| Infrastructure | The gold-pipeline prototype uses Yahoo `GC=F` (COMEX continuous futures) and supports labeled local CSV input. HGB has the lowest holdout MAE (0.002418) on 761 dates; ranking is descriptive. Forecast-error variance in predicted Q5 is about 9–15 times Q1. Segmented high-vol parameters raised MAE; log-target $\exp(\mu+\sigma^{2}/2)$ cut bias but not Q5 variance. Student-t six-model holdout CSV is still missing. | Fill AI and contribution placeholders. ## GARCH estimation update

- At every origin, fit returns scaled by their historical root mean square and convert forecast variance back to original units.
- All 445 fits passed convergence and parameter-constraint checks. Optimizer bounds-clipping warnings occurred during intermediate steps; convergence does not prove a global optimum.
- In the earlier 20-model comparison, GARCH had the lowest point MSE and RMSE; HAR had the lowest MAE. These rankings are superseded by the expanded 25-model comparison above.
- An exploratory quantile-GARCH case adds an extra squared-return response above the historical 95th percentile of absolute returns. At the 2026-11-03 origin, its constrained tail coefficient was approximately zero; statistical significance remains untested. The integrated comparison includes its forecasts where fits succeeded.

## Data readiness

- Keir selected gold futures as the Stage 2 working instrument; the current pipeline uses Yahoo Finance **`GC=F`**, a COMEX gold futures continuous series, not a single fixed-expiry contract. This does not settle a contract-specific strategy or license/redistribution rights.
- Yahoo Finance `XAUUSD=X` returned no data in the check recorded on 2026-11-06; `GC=F` was verified to return daily observations.
- The candidate panel uses Yahoo `DX-Y.NYB` (DXY), `^GSPC` (S&P 500 price index and derived close-to-close log return), `^VIX`, and `GC=F` volume when returned; FRED `DGS10`, `T10YIE`, and `DCOILWTICO`. FRED values are assigned a one-business-day availability proxy, not a series-specific release timestamp or historical vintage; Yahoo closes are aligned to the same date under the after-market-publication forecast origin.
- A separate LSEG import uses only `GCc1` for the gold target and assigns predictors to the next weekday after observation as an availability proxy. The current local export has no `ACVOL_1`, breakeven-inflation, or WTI file; LSEG spot/fixing requests failed. It produced 4,058 five-session forecast origins through 2026-11-03 and includes additional option-quote columns. This is a partial alternative dataset, not a replacement for the selected seven-variable panel or a model decision.
- Central-bank gold demand is deferred until a source and publication schedule support point-in-time alignment. Gold volume is optional and is a continuous-futures series measure, not a fixed-contract or exchange-wide volume measure.
- Raw downloads, prepared data, and manifests remain under Git-ignored `data/`. FRED series are downloaded as public CSVs without an API key. Check source-specific redistribution terms before committing any CSV; file size does not establish permission.
- The current prototype uses a five-observation forward realized-variance label by default; confirm the target definition and horizon before treating results as project decisions or fixing pipeline requirements.

## Git submissions by team member

The table and commit list below are generated from `git log --all` when this deck is rendered. With the main-only workflow, they show commits reachable from the locally available `main` history, attributed using the author identities mapped below. They do not count uncommitted changes or independently enumerate GitHub PRs. Fetch `main` before rendering so recent submissions appear.

```{python}
import subprocess

team_aliases = {
    "Keir": {"0keirli0", "keir"},
    "Enoch": {"enoch1uo", "enoch"},
    "Samuel": {"samuel"},
}

result = subprocess.run(
    [
        "git",
        "log",
        "--all",
        "--date=short",
        "--format=%h%x09%an%x09%ad%x09%s",
    ],
    check=True,
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)

commits = []
for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
    commit_hash, author, commit_date, subject = line.split("\t", maxsplit=3)
    normalized_author = author.strip().casefold()
    member = next(
        (
            name
            for name, aliases in team_aliases.items()
            if normalized_author in aliases
        ),
        author,
    )
    commits.append(
        {
            "Member / author": member,
            "Commit": commit_hash,
            "Date": commit_date,
            "Submission": subject,
        }
    )

if not commits:
    print("No commits are visible in the current repository refs.")
else:
    counts = {member: 0 for member in team_aliases}
    latest = {member: "—" for member in team_aliases}
    for commit in commits:
        member = commit["Member / author"]
        if member in counts:
            counts[member] += 1
            if latest[member] == "—":
                latest[member] = f'{commit["Date"]} ({commit["Commit"]})'

    print("| Member | Visible commits | Latest visible commit |")
    print("|---|---:|---|")
    for member in team_aliases:
        print(f"| {member} | {counts[member]} | {latest[member]} |")

    print("\nRecent submissions visible in Git history:")
    print("| Author | Commit | Date | Submission |")
    print("|---|---|---|---|")
    for commit in commits[:12]:
        subject = commit["Submission"].replace("|", "\\|")
        print(
            f'| {commit["Member / author"]} | {commit["Commit"]} '
            f'| {commit["Date"]} | {subject} |'
        )
```

Before rendering, fetch the shared `main` branch so the report includes its latest commits:
